content_units: You already have a base in descriptive statistics and basic probability, so this plan prioritizes   confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, and exam-style problem solving  . With your available time, you have about   25.5 study hours   over 21 days, which is enough for a solid pass target of   80%+   if you stay consistent.
Week   Dates   Focus   Key Sessions   Goal/Quiz

Week 1   Days 1-7   Core foundations and distributions   Review mean/median/SD; probability rules; random variables; normal distribution; sampling ideas; standard error   Solve a 20-25 question mixed basics set with   70%+

Week 2   Days 8-14   Confidence intervals and hypothesis testing   Build CI intuition; z vs t; one-sample tests; p-values; Type I/II errors; test setup practice   Complete a timed set on CIs/tests with   75%+

Week 3   Days 15-21   Common exam problems and final revision   Two-sample ideas; categorical tests if included; interpretation traps; formula recall; timed mixed papers; light review last 3 days   Full mixed mock and targeted correction to reach   80% level
- Review: mean, median, mode, range, variance, standard deviation
- Focus on when each measure is appropriate
- Probability refresher: independent events, conditional probability, complements
- Practice translating words into probability notation
- Practice converting values to z-scores and interpreting area/probability
- Population vs sample, parameter vs statistic
- Standard error and why sample means vary
- Intro link between sampling and confidence intervals
- 60-75 minutes of mixed practice from Days 1-5
- Error log: write down every mistake type
- Timed quiz: descriptive stats + probability + normal + sampling
- Milestone: be comfortable with notation, z-scores, and standard error intuition
Week 2: Confidence intervals and hypothesis testing
- Margin of error, confidence level, sample size effects
- One-sample confidence intervals for a mean
- z-interval vs t-interval at intro level
- Practice full writeups: hypotheses, calculation, decision, conclusion
- Type I and Type II errors
- Relationship between CI and hypothesis testing
- Review every missed question by category:
- Milestone: correctly identify and solve standard CI/test questions with   75%+
Week 3: Exam scoring and final polish
- Two-sample comparisons if included in your course
- Difference in means/proportions at a basic level
- Learn the pattern, not every edge case
- If not included, use this day for extra hypothesis test practice
- Correlation and simple regression interpretation if part of syllabus
- Practice reading output and avoiding causation mistakes
- Create final “must-fix” list of 5-8 recurring issues
- Finish with 30-45 min formula recall drill
- Review summary sheet and error log
- Milestone: calm, accurate, and ready for an   80%+   attempt
-   End of Week 1:   You can compute and interpret z-scores, standard deviation, standard error, and sampling concepts without confusion.
-   End of Week 2:   You can choose and solve basic confidence interval and hypothesis test questions, then explain the result clearly in words.
-   End of Week 3:   You can complete a mixed timed paper with controlled mistakes and strong performance on your core topics.
Keep this phase light so you stay sharp rather than overloaded.
-   Day 19:   Target only your weakest 2-3 topics; redo previously missed problems.
-   Day 20:   Review your one-page sheet, formulas, and interpretation phrases; do a short untimed set.
-   Day 21:   No heavy studying; only quick recall, a few easy problems, and rest.
Use the   60-30-10 rule   for each of the last 3 days:
-   60%   reviewing worked examples and your error log
Option 1: Error Log Method   Best for reaching 80% fast   Focus on repeated mistakes
Option 2: Timed Mixed Practice   Best for exam readiness   Builds speed and question recognition
Option 3: One-Page Summary Sheet   Best for confidence intervals and tests   Improves recall under pressure
